propositions: Type-tier comparability for blocking links produces incorrect escalation and ancestor self-blocks: task and story children of the same epic cannot link directly because promotion fails to find a comparable-tier ancestor and falls back to the epic, creating an epic-blocks-child edge
Redundancy validation occurs before promotion on the original pair, so a direct task-to-story link that resolves to an epic-to-child edge escapes the redundancy guard that should reject it
Structural comparability based on parent hierarchy and nearest common ancestor enables correct promotion and allows recomputation of redundancy from the resolved pair
A virtual-root sentinel appended to ancestor chains eliminates the undefined disjoint-tree case and treats parentless tickets as siblings
The widened redundancy predicate rejects any blocking pair whose resolved endpoints are in an ancestor-descendant relationship, subsumes the direct parent-child case, and prevents the 1803 bug
Non-blocking relations retain the original-pair redundancy check and gain no new rejections despite the widened blocking predicate
